title: The circle
goals: A trial of one of the six kinds in the circle.
starting_code:
# Describe your kind of familiar with `class` and `(Familiar)`, empty for now, with `pass` under it.

# Make one creature of that class and keep it in a variable.

# Call it into the circle with `cast` and `minka`.
hints: The six kinds in the book are `Fox`, `Crow`, `Bat`, `Hare`, `Mouse` and `Frog`: one of them is your class's name.
An object is made with its class's name and brackets, and kept with `=`, like any value.
Last, `wizard.cast` with two things: `"minka"` and the variable you kept your creature in.
intro: Look: {friend} already has a trial in the circle. Now you: describe a kind of familiar, make one and call it into the circle. The six kinds are in my book.
outro:
Luckily, as long as you do not take it out of the circle, it is only a trial, and it soon vanishes.

Next time you will give it its name and its colour.
learned: Now you know that a class describes a kind of thing, and that an object is one thing made with it, with the class's name and brackets; the variable you keep it in is only what your program calls it.

told.won:
Not bad. At least it is {familiar_a_kind}, yes.

As you see, your familiar vanishes after a few seconds.

It needs a name and a colour to be stable and to stay longer in the circle.
told.bimo: *(Opens one eye, and closes it again.)* Mrrr…
